stem: The phenomenon in which a small fraction of light scattered by a transparent medium changes its wavelength (colour) due to interaction with the molecules of that medium — discovered by an Indian physicist and named National Science Day (28 February) in its honour — is the:
explanation: Sir C.V. Raman discovered (1928) that scattered light changes wavelength on interacting with molecules — the Raman Effect, for which he won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics; National Science Day commemorates the discovery date — distinct from the Tyndall Effect (scattering of light by colloidal particles, without wavelength change).
